# 不做AEO的网站，大脑还在休息：实操清单与衡量方法

作者：@Ruesandora0  
日期：2026-11-03（北京时间）  
来源：[X原帖](https://x.com/Ruesandora0/status/2117286230761378294)  
分类：方法

## 中文全文

# 没做 AEO 的网站，大脑还在休息

向 ChatGPT、Perplexity 或 Google 的 AI Overview 提一个问题，你会得到一个答案。答案里被点名的网站，已经被选中了。下面那些蓝色链接排在其次。AEO 做的，就是争取成为被选中的那个。我把它是什么、什么做法真正有帮助，以及如何衡量，写了下来。

## 什么是 AEO

AEO 是 answer engine optimization，也就是答案引擎优化。它的目标，是在直接回答问题的地方被选中：Google AI Overviews 和精选摘要，以及 ChatGPT、Perplexity、Gemini 的回答。

大多数人用 GEO 和 AEO 指代同一件事。我这样区分：SEO 是提升排名，GEO 和 AEO 是进入答案、获得提及。对于 Google 自己的产品，它并不把这当成一种独立业务。Google 在 2026 年 7 月 10 日更新的指南中说，针对生成式 AI 搜索做优化，仍然是 SEO。

## 答案引擎会选择什么

没有哪个引擎承诺“这样做就会选中你”。Google 表示，你无法决定哪些内容会成为精选摘要，这是由其系统选择的（相关页面最后更新于 2025 年 12 月 10 日）。下面的内容都不是保证，而是让答案更容易被找到的做法。

**把标题写成问题。** 用人们真的会问的一句话作标题，例如“运费是多少？”。标题下面的第一段，就回答这个问题。

**在第一段直接给答案。** 把答案放在第一句话，背景和例外情况放在后面。有从业者建议用 40 到 60 个词。这是从业者的建议，不是 Google 的规则。对我来说，两三句话就够了。

**在句子里重复主体。** 一段话即使被从页面中单独摘出来阅读，也应该说得通。开头写出主体的名称，不要只写“这个”。

**短段落、列表、表格。** 如果有价格、步骤或对比，就用表格或编号列表。有先后顺序的内容放列表，需要比较的内容放表格。

**作者和日期。** 标明是谁写的、什么时候写的，以及什么时候更新的。如果引用来源，要提供网址和日期。只显示日期还不够：如果更新了页面，也要真正更新内容。

**FAQ 和 HowTo 结构化数据。** 有用，但不是必需的。Google 的 AI 指南说，要出现在生成式 AI 功能中，并不需要特殊的 [schema.org](https://schema.org) 标记。如果使用了这类标记，对应文字也必须显示在页面上，结构化数据必须与可见文字一致。

**把内容拆成小块。** 同一份指南说，这也没有必要。它说，人们喜欢用段落和章节组织好的页面。因此，不要刻意把页面切碎，把文章写好就行。

**llms.txt。** 这是放在网站根目录中的 Markdown 文件，用来列出重要页面。它不是官方标准。Google 搜索不使用它。我也没找到公司官方文档，能够证明其他系统会使用它。你当然可以加一个，但它不是 AEO 的核心。

**让机器人能进来。** 机器人读不到页面，就没法引用页面。robots.txt、机器人拦截，以及只有运行 JavaScript 后才显示的内容，都属于这方面的问题。先检查这些，再处理文字内容。

## 一份可以直接复制的检查清单

检查你最重要的 10 个页面：

- 标题是一个真实问题，或者一句清楚的主题句。

- 第一段回答问题，没有铺垫句。

- 段落单独拿出来读，也能说得通。

- 页面各处的价格、时长和条件都一致。

- 有顺序的操作使用编号列表，对比内容使用表格。

- 作者姓名、发布日期和更新日期清晰可见。

- 每个数字旁边都有来源和日期。

- 页面已被索引，允许机器人访问，关闭 JS 后仍能看到内容。

- 如果使用了结构化数据，它与页面可见文字完全一致。

- 没有写任何自己并不知道的事情。

## 常见错误

- 为每个问题都生成一个单独但几乎一样的页面。Google 可能会将这种做法归入其规模化内容滥用政策的处理范围。

- 只向机器人展示答案。不要放隐藏文字。答案应该出现在所有人都能看到的页面上。

- 第一段以“在当今的数字世界里”开头。结果答案被挤到了第三段。

- 设置好了结构化数据，却把正文留空。标记不能替代内容。

- 硬把问答模块塞进首页。一个并非专门回答某个问题的页面，不需要这样的模块。

- 相信那些出售 AEO 服务、声称“保证效果”的人。Google 的指南建议，评估这类服务时，应使用其针对第三方 SEO 建议所给出的同样标准。

## 如何衡量

Search Console 没有专门针对 AI Overviews 的独立报告。根据 Google 的帮助页面，出现在 AI Overviews 和 AI Mode 中的网站，会计入效果报告里的“网页”搜索类型。因此，你不能把这些点击单独拆出来，然后说“这么多来自 AI”。在 GA4 中，Google 的 AI 点击同样记录在 Organic Search（自然搜索）渠道下。

剩下能做的，就是手动衡量提及情况。一般方法如下：

- 写出 20 到 30 个客户真正会问的问题，不要放品牌名。

- 在 ChatGPT、Perplexity、Gemini 和 Google 中逐个提问。

- 对每次回答，分别记录两件事：你的网站是否被列为来源，以及它是否在答案正文中被提及。

- 同一个问题重复问几次。每次答案都会变化。

- 每个月用同一份问题清单重跑一次，带上日期保存。

重复测试和分开记录都很重要。同一个问题，下次可能得到不同答案；被列为来源，也不等于在答案里被点名。因此，不要只凭一次测试就下结论。

来自 [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com) 等来源的访客，可以在 GA4 里单独查看。这反映的是点击，不是提及。

## 最后想说的

答案放在第一段，页面允许机器人访问，日期和作者清楚明确，每个数字都有来源。这些大部分本来就是好的 SEO。新的地方，是到答案内部去寻找结果。

## 外文原文

# the brain of a site without AEO is resting

Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google's AI Overview a question and you get one answer. The site named inside it has been picked. The blue links below it come second. AEO is the work of earning a place in that pick. I wrote down what it is, what actually helps, and how to measure it.

## what is aeo

AEO stands for answer engine optimization. The goal is to be chosen where a question gets answered directly: Google AI Overviews and featured snippets, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini answers.

Most people use GEO and AEO for the same job. I split them like this: SEO is climbing the rankings, GEO and AEO are getting mentioned inside the answer. Google does not treat it as a separate trade for its own surfaces. Its guide, updated on July 10, 2026, says optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO.

## what answer engines pick

No engine promises "do this and you will be picked". Google says you cannot decide what becomes the featured snippet, its systems choose (last updated December 10, 2025). Nothing below is a guarantee. These are the things that make an answer easy to find.

**question-shaped headings.** Write the heading as a sentence people really ask: "how much is shipping?". Make the first paragraph under it the answer to that question.

**the direct answer in the first paragraph.** Put the answer in the first sentence. Background and exceptions come after. Practitioners suggest 40 to 60 words. That is a practitioner suggestion, not a Google rule. Two or three sentences are enough for me.

**repeat the subject in the sentence.** A paragraph should make sense if it is lifted out of the page and read alone. Start with the name of the subject, not with "this".

**short paragraphs, lists, tables.** If you have prices, steps or a comparison, use a table or a numbered list. Things with an order go in a list, things you compare go in a table.

**author and date.** Show who wrote it, when it was written and when it was updated. If you cite a source, give the address and the date. Showing a date is not enough: if you updated the page, update the content too.

**faq and howto structured data.** Useful, but not required. Google's AI guide says no special [schema.org](https://schema.org) markup is needed to appear in generative AI features. If you use it, the text must also be visible on the page, and the structured data must match the visible text.

**splitting content into chunks.** The same guide says this is not needed either. It says people like pages organized with paragraphs and sections. So do not chop the page up, just write it well.

**llms.txt.** A Markdown file in the root directory that lists important pages. It is not an official standard. Google Search does not use it. I could not find a company document showing that other systems use it. You are free to add one, but it is not the main part of AEO.

**keeping the door open for bots.** A bot that cannot read the page cannot cite it. robots.txt, bot blocking and content that only appears after JavaScript all belong here. Check these first, then move on to the text.

## a checklist you can copy

For your 10 most important pages:

- the heading is a real question or a clear topic sentence

- the first paragraph answers the question, with no warm-up sentence

- the paragraph makes sense read on its own

- price, duration and conditions are the same everywhere on the page

- ordered work is in a numbered list, comparisons are in a table

- author name, publish date and update date are visible

- every number has a source and a date next to it

- the page is indexed and open to bots, and the content shows with JS off

- if you used structured data, it matches the visible text exactly

- nothing is written that you do not know

## common mistakes

- Producing a separate, near-identical page for every question. Google can link this to its scaled content abuse policy.

- Showing the answer only to bots. There is no hidden text. The answer belongs on the page everyone sees.

- Opening the first paragraph with "in the digital world today". The answer gets pushed to the third paragraph.

- Setting up structured data and leaving the text empty. Markup does not replace content.

- Forcing a Q&A block onto the home page. A page that does not answer a single question does not need the block.

- Believing someone who sells AEO and says "guaranteed". Google's guide suggests judging these services by the same criteria it gives for third-party SEO advice.

## how to measure it

Search Console has no separate report for AI Overviews. According to Google's help page, sites that appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode are counted in the Performance report under the "Web" search type. So you cannot split out those clicks and say "this much came from AI". In GA4 too, Google's AI clicks are recorded under Organic Search.

What is left is measuring mentions by hand. The general method:

- Write 20 to 30 questions your customer would really ask. Leave out the brand name.

- Ask each question in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google.

- For each answer, log two things separately: was your site listed as a source, and was it mentioned in the answer text.

- Repeat the same question several times. Answers change every time.

- Rerun it with the same list once a month and keep it with the date.

Repeating and separating matter. The same question can get a different answer on the next try, and being listed as a source is not the same as being named in the answer. So do not draw a conclusion from one try.

Visitors from sources like [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com) can be seen separately in GA4. That shows clicks, not mentions.

## last word

The answer to the question is in the first paragraph, the page is open to bots, the date and author are clear, and every number has a source. Most of this is already good SEO. What is new is looking for the result inside the answer.
